newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks close weaker after digesting gains.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks close weaker after digesting gains.

* Toronto stocks sank on Wednesday as investors paused to take profits and digest recent gains. * Almost all 14 groups fell. * 91 million shares traded worth C$1.6 billion.
Toronto's stock market closed weaker for a second straight session on Wednesday as investors took profits following the market's recent new highs.
The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index fell 53.51 points to 6389.03 on Wednesday. Canada's biggest equity market has shed more than 100 points over the past two sessions.
"The market had a good run. It needed to digest it," said Calgary-based portfolio manager Josef Schachter.
The key index soared to a life-time high of 6401.13 points on Monday.

Schachter predicted Toronto would rebound if upcoming U.S. economic data showed that the U.S. economy is growing at a steady pace. That would reduce the need for the Federal Reserve to raise U.S. interest rates and allow Canadian rates to remain low.
All but two of Toronto's 14 sub-sectors lost ground, led by oils, golds, conglomerates and utilities. The two gainers were retail and transportation.
Declining issues outnumbered advances 539 to 427 with 310 stocks unchanged.
--- HOT STOCKS ---
* High technology firm Newbridge Networks Corp fell 0.40 to close at 57.10 on 2.2 million shares after hitting new highs earlier in the day.
The telecommunications equipment firm hit a 52-week peak of 60 after New York-based brokerage Alex. Brown upgraded the stock to a stronger buy from a buy.
* Royal Bank of Canada, the nation's largest bank, slipped 0.10 to 60.80 in active dealings after reporting higher second quarter profits on Wednesday.
